## 1. Sri Lanka’s High Court Trial-at-Bar (a special High Court bench that hears a case with three judges) sentenced 15 people over the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks.

Judges Navaratne Marasinghe, Ramanathan Kannan and Sujeewa Nishshanka delivered prison terms that ranged from <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">200 to 260 years</span> per convict, ordered to run across incident blocks consecutively and within each block concurrently. The bench also directed the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">forfeiture of movable and immovable property</span> under the Prevention of Terrorism Act and the Customs-style confiscation provisions triggered by terrorism financing findings.

The indictment carried <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">23,270 counts</span>, and the Trial-at-Bar concluded after hearing <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">2,309 witnesses</span> over nearly five years. Nine defendants were acquitted, and productions ran to 2,076 items, including explosives, precursor chemicals, firearms and digital media used to establish participation and conspiracy.

## 2. Fitch upgraded Sri Lanka’s long-term foreign-currency rating to ‘B-’ with a Stable Outlook.

The agency said stronger revenue and a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">primary surplus of 2.6 percent of GDP</span> in 2026 supported the move from ‘CCC+’, though debt at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">92.9 percent of GDP</span> still far exceeds the roughly 55 percent median for ‘B’ peers. It projected reserves near US$ 7.7 billion by end‑2026, equal to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">about 2.9 months</span> of current external payments, compared with deeper buffers among similarly rated sovereigns.

Fitch described the Long-Term Issuer Default Rating (a sovereign credit rating scale used to signal default risk over a long horizon) improvement as recognition of macro‑stabilisation, while flagging energy‑price shocks as a risk that could push the current account into a 1.2 percent of GDP deficit after three years of surpluses. It warned that <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">interest-to-revenue near 41 percent</span> in 2026 is over three times the ‘B’ median, underscoring the need to sustain fiscal discipline into 2027 and beyond.

## 3. The Supreme Court held that the 22nd Amendment did not require a referendum.

Parliament scheduled a two‑day debate for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">September 24–25</span>, with a vote anticipated the second evening. The Court also directed textual changes, including replacing a Sinhala phrase in Clause 2 and inserting a proviso to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">exempt the sitting Chief Justice</span> from the proposed six‑year limit tied to age 67.

The determination stated that no provision triggered <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Article 83</span> (a constitutional provision that requires a nationwide vote for specified changes), while a companion Judicature (Amendment) Bill could pass by <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">simple majority</span>. The package raises retirement ages at the superior courts and expands appellate capacity, aiming to ease delays by allowing regional Courts of Appeal.

## 4. An IMF team concluded its visit after the seventh review and the 2026 Article IV Consultation.

The mission noted <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">4.2 percent year‑on‑year growth</span> in the second quarter and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">inflation at 8 percent</span> in August amid higher global oil prices, with gross official reserves at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">US$ 6.9 billion</span>. It highlighted risks from the Middle East conflict, El Niño and trade fragmentation, while acknowledging 11 consecutive quarters of expansion.

Staff urged a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">medium‑term revenue strategy</span> and continued price‑stability focus, alongside exchange‑rate flexibility and stronger buffers under the Extended Fund Facility (an IMF lending arrangement that supports multi‑year economic programs). It also called for safeguarding governance reforms and improving social targeting as debt restructuring nears completion.

## 5. Sri Lanka connected its first grid‑scale BESS in Anuradhapura and a 5 MW floating solar plant in Dambulla.

The <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">10 MW/40 MWh</span> Battery Energy Storage System (BESS, a large battery installation that stores electricity for later use) began feeding the grid, while a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">5 MW floating array</span> was commissioned to deliver <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">roughly 9 GWh annually</span> and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">avoid about 6,400 tonnes of CO₂</span>. Together they add flexibility to shift surplus daytime solar into evening peaks and reduce fossil generation costs.

## 6. The Central Bank secured court‑confirmed freezing orders on six companies and their directors over suspected unauthorised deposit‑taking.

Orders obtained under the Finance Business Act froze assets while investigations proceed, with four firms already found to have breached <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Section 2</span> and two under probe. A <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">freezing order</span> (a court order that bars a person or company from disposing of assets) was extended by the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Colombo High Court</span> as the regulator warned savers to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">verify authorisation</span> before placing funds.

## 7. Authorities issued landslide and flood alerts as heavy rain persisted across multiple river basins.

The Irrigation Department reported <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">100–125 mm</span> in the upper Kelani and minor flooding on <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Kuda Ganga at Millakanda</span> near the 6.50 m level, while stations on the Gin and Nilwala showed rising trends. The National Building Research Organisation extended <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Level‑3 landslide warnings</span> in districts including Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Ratnapura, Kalutara and Galle as the Met Department forecast isolated <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">falls above 100 mm</span> and gusts of 40–50 km/h.

## 8. The Government retooled frontline wildlife resources to maintain 5,741 km of electric fencing.

Motorcycles were assigned so a single regulator can patrol <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">roughly 40 km</span> of fencing, alongside 16 double‑cabs, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">84 single‑cabs</span>, nine field tractors and three deep‑forest vehicles redeployed to range and beat offices. The programme, funded via the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Wildlife Preservation Fund</span>, also equipped regional veterinary units and the Elephant Transit Home to speed emergency treatment.

## 9. Parliament approved a Rs 17.213 billion supplementary estimate to fund electricity bill relief.

The in‑year allocation will be met by shifting <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">under‑utilised provisions</span> among line ministries without breaching the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Appropriation Act’s expenditure ceiling</span> or the borrowing limit. The <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Committee on Public Finance</span> cleared the Supplementary Estimate (an additional budget request within a fiscal year) before the vote.

## 10. Police said they would introduce roadside drug‑testing kits for drivers within three months.

The plan follows mandatory medical testing after serious crashes and a night inspection that found <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">more than 5 percent</span> of checked buses operating with drivers <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">under the influence of narcotics</span>. A roadside drug test (an <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">on‑site screening</span> for narcotics using saliva or similar samples) is intended to complement breath tests and target a rising share of severe collisions linked to drugs.
